a novel ankle rehabilitation device based on a high performance parallel mechanism is presented.

the development of a high performance robotic platform for ankle rehabilitation.

the design and development of a high-performance 2-dof ankle rehabilitation robotic device that can be used in clinical settings for the treatment of patients with ankle injuries and/or neurological diseases.

this paper proposes a novel ankle rehabilitation robotic device that is capable of performing all the exercises required for ankle rehabilitation and is based on a 3-RRR over-actuated mechanism that is capable of eliminating the singularities and improving the dexterity of the system.
the presented device is a promising candidate to be used in the clinical environment.
the proposed design is able to satisfy the requirements for high performance ankle rehabilitation devices while being compact, light-weight and easy to manufacture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a high performance ankle rehabilitation device based on a novel 2-dof parallel mechanism.
the device is able to perform all the exercises required for ankle rehabilitation and it is also capable of carrying out exercises for the rehabilitation of the foot, the knee and the hip.
the proposed device is a high performance ankle rehabilitation platform, which has the advantage of compactness and dexterity over the existing ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cable driven linear actuators is a viable alternative for the design of high torque capacity, low weight and back-drivable rehabilitation robots.
a high performance ankle rehabilitation device can be designed and built with a very compact and simple architecture.
a simple parallel mechanism can be made to achieve a high degree of dexterity while at the same being compact and capable of carrying out the full range of ankle rehabilitation exercises.
